component.name: azure-storage-queue
component.title: Azure Storage Queue Service
component.description: Send messages to and receive messages from the queues of Azure Queue Storage.
component.label: cloud,messaging

configuration.description: The configuration that each endpoint of the component starts from, as a copy. The options of the endpoint replace its values.

credentialType.label: common
credentialType.description: How the client authenticates when serviceClient is not set. SHARED_ACCOUNT_KEY and SHARED_KEY_CREDENTIAL both use the credentials option if it is set, and otherwise accountName and accessKey. AZURE_IDENTITY uses the DefaultAzureCredential of azure-identity, which takes the identity from environment variables, a managed identity or a developer tool login. If not set, SHARED_KEY_CREDENTIAL is used when credentials is set, and otherwise SHARED_ACCOUNT_KEY.

serviceClient.label: common
serviceClient.description: To use a custom com.azure.storage.queue.QueueServiceClient for the requests to the queue service. When this option is set or autowired, the client brings the address and the authentication, and the accountName, credentialType, accessKey and credentials options are not used to connect.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

createQueue.label: producer
createQueue.description: Whether sendMessage first creates the queue if it does not exist, with the metadata of the CamelAzureStorageQueueMetadata header. The CamelAzureStorageQueueCreateQueue header replaces this option.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

operation.label: producer
operation.description: The operation that the producer performs. The CamelAzureStorageQueueOperation header replaces this option. If neither is set, the producer performs sendMessage.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

healthCheckConsumerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckConsumerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all consumer based health checks from this component

healthCheckProducerEnabled.label: health
healthCheckProducerEnabled.description: Used for enabling or disabling all producer based health checks from this component. Notice: Camel has by default disabled all producer based health-checks. You can turn on producer checks globally by setting camel.health.producersEnabled=true.

maxMessages.label: queue
maxMessages.description: The maximum number of messages to receive, from 1 to 32: in each poll of the consumer, and for receiveMessages and peekMessages. The CamelAzureStorageQueueMaxMessages header replaces this option for the producer.

messageId.label: queue
messageId.description: The ID of the message that deleteMessage or updateMessage changes. The CamelAzureStorageQueueMessageId header, which the consumer and sendMessage set, replaces this option.

popReceipt.label: queue
popReceipt.description: The pop receipt of the message that deleteMessage or updateMessage changes, which must be the latest pop receipt of that message. The CamelAzureStorageQueuePopReceipt header, which the consumer, sendMessage and updateMessage set to the pop receipt they get, replaces this option.

timeout.label: queue
timeout.description: The time, for example PT10S or 10s, within which each request of the producer and the consumer to the queue service must complete, or it fails with an exception. If not set, only the timeouts of the HTTP client apply. The CamelAzureStorageQueueTimeout header replaces this option for the producer.

timeToLive.label: queue
timeToLive.description: How long the message that sendMessage sends stays in the queue, for example P2D or 12h, in whole seconds. If not set, the queue service keeps it for 7 days, and PT-1S keeps it until it is deleted. The CamelAzureStorageQueueTimeToLive header replaces this option.

visibilityTimeout.label: queue
visibilityTimeout.description: How long a message stays invisible in the queue, for example PT30S or 30s, in whole seconds and at most 7 days. sendMessage hides the message it sends for this long, or not at all if not set, and updateMessage, which requires it, hides the message for this long from the update. receiveMessages and the consumer hide each message they receive for this long, or 30 seconds if not set, and the consumer receives a message again after this time if its exchange failed. The CamelAzureStorageQueueVisibilityTimeout header replaces this option for the producer.

accessKey.label: security
accessKey.description: The account key of the storage account, which authenticates the client together with accountName when credentialType is SHARED_ACCOUNT_KEY or SHARED_KEY_CREDENTIAL. Not used when the credentials option or the serviceClient option is set.

credentials.label: security
credentials.description: To use a com.azure.storage.common.StorageSharedKeyCredential, which holds the account name and an account key of the storage account, when credentialType is SHARED_KEY_CREDENTIAL or SHARED_ACCOUNT_KEY. When it is set, the accountName and accessKey options are not used to authenticate. Not used when serviceClient is set.

CamelAzureStorageQueueRawHttpHeaders.description: The HTTP headers of the response of the queue service, as a com.azure.core.http.HttpHeaders. The producer sets it for each operation except listQueues, receiveMessages and peekMessages.

CamelAzureStorageQueueMetadata.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueMetadata.description: The metadata of the queue that createQueue creates, or that sendMessage creates when createQueue is true. sendMessage does not change the metadata of a queue that already exists.

CamelAzureStorageQueueMessageId.description: The ID of the message. The consumer sets it for each message it receives, and sendMessage for the message it sends. It replaces the messageId option for deleteMessage and updateMessage.

CamelAzureStorageQueueInsertionTime.description: The time the message was added to the queue. The consumer and sendMessage set it.

CamelAzureStorageQueueExpirationTime.description: The time the message expires and the queue service deletes it. The consumer and sendMessage set it.

CamelAzureStorageQueuePopReceipt.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueuePopReceipt.description: The pop receipt of the message, which deleteMessage and updateMessage need, and which is no longer valid once the message is received again or updated. The consumer, sendMessage and updateMessage set it to the pop receipt they get. It replaces the popReceipt option for deleteMessage and updateMessage.

CamelAzureStorageQueueTimeNextVisible.description: The time the message becomes visible in the queue again. The consumer, sendMessage and updateMessage set it.

CamelAzureStorageQueueDequeueCount.description: The number of times the message has been received from the queue, this time included. The consumer sets it.

CamelAzureStorageQueueConsumedQueueName.label: consumer
CamelAzureStorageQueueConsumedQueueName.description: The name of the queue the message was received from. It is not the CamelAzureStorageQueueName header, which overrides the queue of a producer.

CamelAzureStorageQueueOperation.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueOperation.description: The operation that the producer performs. It replaces the operation option.

CamelAzureStorageQueueName.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueName.description: The name of the queue for the producer. It replaces the queueName option.

CamelAzureStorageQueueSegmentOptions.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueSegmentOptions.description: The options of listQueues: the prefix of the names of the queues to list, whether to include the metadata of each queue, and the number of queues per page. If not set, listQueues lists all queues without their metadata.

CamelAzureStorageQueueTimeout.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueTimeout.description: The time within which each request of the producer to the queue service must complete, or it fails with an exception. It replaces the timeout option.

CamelAzureStorageQueueMaxMessages.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueMaxMessages.description: The maximum number of messages that receiveMessages or peekMessages returns, from 1 to 32. It replaces the maxMessages option.

CamelAzureStorageQueueVisibilityTimeout.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueVisibilityTimeout.description: How long the message stays invisible in the queue, at most 7 days: the message that sendMessage sends, each message that receiveMessages receives, or the message that updateMessage updates, for which it is required. It replaces the visibilityTimeout option.

CamelAzureStorageQueueTimeToLive.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueTimeToLive.description: How long the message that sendMessage sends stays in the queue, where PT-1S keeps it until it is deleted. It replaces the timeToLive option.

CamelAzureStorageQueueCreateQueue.label: producer
CamelAzureStorageQueueCreateQueue.description: Whether sendMessage first creates the queue if it does not exist. It replaces the createQueue option.

consumerOut.description: The text of the queue message as a stream, with its id and pop receipt in headers; no body for a message without text

producerIn.description: The text of the message for sendMessage, the default, and updateMessage: bytes, a stream or a file are read as text, and a Map or a POJO is sent as its toString(): marshal it first. sendMessage fails without a body, and updateMessage then changes only the visibility. The other operations do not use the body

producerOut.description: true after sendMessage, the default, and the operations that create, clear, update or delete, with their results in headers, such as the id and the pop receipt of the message sent. A List of the items of the SDK for listQueues, receiveMessages and peekMessages

accountName.description: The name of the Azure Storage account, which gives the address https://accountName.queue.core.windows.net of its queue service. If the credentials option is set, the account name of those credentials gives the address instead. Not used when serviceClient is set.

queueName.description: The name of the queue. Required for the consumer and for each producer operation except listQueues. The CamelAzureStorageQueueName header replaces this option for the producer.

credentialType.label: common
credentialType.description: How the client authenticates when serviceClient is not set. SHARED_ACCOUNT_KEY and SHARED_KEY_CREDENTIAL both use the credentials option if it is set, and otherwise accountName and accessKey. AZURE_IDENTITY uses the DefaultAzureCredential of azure-identity, which takes the identity from environment variables, a managed identity or a developer tool login. If not set, SHARED_KEY_CREDENTIAL is used when credentials is set, and otherwise SHARED_ACCOUNT_KEY.

serviceClient.label: common
serviceClient.description: To use a custom com.azure.storage.queue.QueueServiceClient for the requests to the queue service. When this option is set or autowired, the client brings the address and the authentication, and the accountName, credentialType, accessKey and credentials options are not used to connect.

sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.label: consumer
sendEmptyMessageWhenIdle.description: If the polling consumer did not poll any files, you can enable this option to send an empty message (no body) instead.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

pollStrategy.label: consumer,advanced
pollStrategy.description: A pluggable org.apache.camel.PollingConsumerPollingStrategy allowing you to provide your custom implementation to control error handling usually occurred during the poll operation before an Exchange have been created and being routed in Camel.

backoffErrorThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffErrorThreshold.description: The number of subsequent error polls (failed due some error) that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffIdleThreshold.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffIdleThreshold.description: The number of subsequent idle polls that should happen before the backoffMultipler should kick-in.

backoffMultiplier.label: consumer,scheduler
backoffMultiplier.description: To let the scheduled polling consumer backoff if there has been a number of subsequent idles/errors in a row. The multiplier is then the number of polls that will be skipped before the next actual attempt is happening again. When this option is in use then backoffIdleThreshold and/or backoffErrorThreshold must also be configured.

greedy.label: consumer,scheduler
greedy.description: If greedy is enabled, then the ScheduledPollConsumer will run immediately again, if the previous run polled 1 or more messages.

healthCheckMaxPollDuration.label: consumer,scheduler
healthCheckMaxPollDuration.description: How long a poll may run before the health check of the consumer reports DOWN. The health check is otherwise based on the polls that are done, so it stays UP while a poll hangs, for example on a read without timeout from a connection that went silent. A poll includes routing the messages it polled, so set this above the longest poll you expect. The poll is not interrupted. The value is in millis (not affected by timeUnit). The default 0 turns this off.

initialDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
initialDelay.description: Milliseconds before the first poll starts.

repeatCount.label: consumer,scheduler
repeatCount.description: Specifies a maximum limit of number of fires. So if you set it to 1, the scheduler will only fire once. If you set it to 5, it will only fire five times. A value of zero or negative means fire forever.

runLoggingLevel.label: consumer,scheduler
runLoggingLevel.description: The consumer logs a start/complete log line when it polls. This option allows you to configure the logging level for that.

scheduledExecutorService.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduledExecutorService.description: Allows for configuring a custom/shared thread pool to use for the consumer. By default each consumer has its own single threaded thread pool.

scheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
scheduler.description: To use a cron scheduler from either camel-spring or camel-quartz component. Use value spring or quartz for built in scheduler

schedulerProperties.label: consumer,scheduler
schedulerProperties.description: To configure additional properties when using a custom scheduler or any of the Quartz, Spring based scheduler. This is a multi-value option with prefix: scheduler.

startScheduler.label: consumer,scheduler
startScheduler.description: Whether the scheduler should be auto started.

timeUnit.label: consumer,scheduler
timeUnit.description: Time unit for initialDelay and delay options.

useFixedDelay.label: consumer,scheduler
useFixedDelay.description: Controls if fixed delay or fixed rate is used. See ScheduledExecutorService in JDK for details.

accessKey.description: The account key of the storage account, which authenticates the client together with accountName when credentialType is SHARED_ACCOUNT_KEY or SHARED_KEY_CREDENTIAL. Not used when the credentials option or the serviceClient option is set.
